summary.title: Feature flags are ruining your codebase
summary.one_liner: Feature flags are useful, but letting PMs control them without discipline adds complexity, dead code and testing burden, so classify each toggle and enforce its removal.
takeaways: Feature flags start as release toggles but tend to multiply once PMs use them for per-user access, A/B tests, ops kill switches and premium tiers.
Each flag carries a cost: harder code comprehension, dead latent code, and a testing burden that grows with every flag combination.
Classify toggles into release, ops, experiment and permission types, since each has a different lifespan and owner.
Enforce removal with expiration dates, time-bomb tests that fail after expiry, or a cap on the number of active flags.
Use an existing standard such as OpenFeature rather than building your own flag system.
summary.summary: An opinion piece by an engineer who argues that feature flags are good but get overused once product managers take control of them. It walks through the uses that accumulate (release, ops, experiment and permission toggles), the costs they add to code complexity, dead code and testing, and a real example of a flag that was never released. It draws on Pete Hodgson's article on Martin Fowler's site for the toggle taxonomy and suggests managing each category with its own owner and lifespan, plus ways to force removal of old flags.
